INOD is a speculative-shadow candidate for data readiness, model evaluation, and AI quality assurance; survival requires verification of customer independence, revenue durability, and cash conversion.

Next pass should test revenue quality across AI/cloud software names: customer concentration, related-party or investment-linked demand, credits, gross margin, RPO, deferred revenue, and operating cash flow.

DOMO is a speculative_shadow exception below the preferred market-cap range; keep only if future filings show retention, cash-flow, and AI adoption improvement.

Layer 2 should explicitly test revenue quality for software/cloud AI claims: independent customer demand, related-party or investment-funded spend, gross margin, free cash flow, customer concentration, and whether AI revenue is separately disclosed.

AVPT should remain in the underfollowed AI software/data-readiness lane because its governance, access-control, auditability, and resilience products map directly to enterprise AI deployment prerequisites.

BBAI belongs in speculative_shadow rather than core underfollowed due to stronger narrative risk, government-contract lumpiness, and need to verify revenue quality and cash conversion.

For AI software, the bottleneck screen should prioritize data governance, regulated deployment, workflow integration, observability/security, auditability, and independent revenue quality over generic AI marketing language.

Later layers should explicitly test whether AI-related software revenue is separately disclosed, whether customers are independent, and whether net retention/gross margin/free cash flow support claims of AI-driven adoption.
APPN added as underfollowed AI workflow/governance candidate; key survival test is whether AI features materially improve subscription growth, retention, regulated-industry wins, and cash conversion.
PATH added as underfollowed agentic automation/orchestration candidate; key survival test is ARR acceleration, net retention, production AI-agent deployments, and margin discipline.

For AI software, the likely chokepoint is not model access alone but the governed conversion of enterprise data into auditable, secure, production workflows.

Cloud revenue quality should remain a separate falsification workstream; future layers should check whether reported AI/cloud growth is arm's-length demand or partly influenced by vendor investments, credits, or commercial entanglements.

node: AI software, automation, data platforms, and cloud revenue quality
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Layer 1B expansion for the AI software/data-workflow node finds one high-attention reference leader, one large-cap observability platform, and two smaller direct-exposure candidates. The chokepoint is not generic model access; it is governed enterprise deployment: data readiness, LLM observability, workflow orchestration, safety/evaluation, and auditability. Revenue-quality diligence remains critical because AI software claims can be easier to overstate than physical infrastructure bottlenecks. This pass expands the AI software/data-workflow chokepoint universe around enterprise data readiness, auditability, observability, governed analytics, and revenue-quality risk. The list deliberately keeps one high-attention reference name for AI observability context, then shifts to lower-attention or messier-label software companies where the AI linkage is plausible but must be verified through retention, independent customer demand, product-level adoption, gross margin, cash conversion, and disclosure quality. No candidate here is a trading recommendation. Expanded the AI software/data-workflow node with a two-lane universe: one high-attention reference anchor and three smaller discovery names. The underfollowed lane emphasizes data governance, regulated workflow deployment, vertical banking software, and defense/regulatory AI decision systems rather than generic chatbot/model exposure. Key falsification risk: AI positioning may be marketing-led unless revenue quality, retention, independent customers, gross margin, and cash conversion confirm product-level adoption. Expanded the A
